reasoning: Set A wins on content; structure ties. Its spec is far more rigorous and stays true to the ground truth. Every environment has exact rules, observations and rewards, with worked numbers that check out (1.99/1/0 returns, 0.798 energy, starving at step 500). The policy-gradient ladder, ablation switches, self-play schedules and cross-play table cover every concept the user named. It keeps to free tools only and to beating both random and scripted baselines. Its nine milestones repeat one clean pattern per stage (train → baselines/curves/replay → study), and each Depends cell is real. A's weaknesses are size and leftovers. The architecture still carries replan narration ('Docs to rework… the build waits for… replan', 'M1 has 0 of 22 tasks done'). The brief still says 'The second environment, whatever it is'. Rewards and observations are missing from its spec. Its pipelines still point to the uninstalled skills that AD-20/AD-21 replaced. Its training spines say 'time-boxed' / 'until the time limit', which contradicts AD-18's step budget. M3 and M4 are lumpy single milestones with no Skills or References lines, and M3 bundles the single-fish and five-fish tanks even though DONE-04 makes the second wait on the first. Its M1-T05 packet asks for the whole Double DQN plus its training loop as an XS task, with no hyperparameter values given.
